source.title: Over-training with Mixup May Hurt Generalization

record.tranche_reason: It measures test performance over training time and reports a fall-then-rise generalization pattern under Mixup, using its own over-training experiments rather than reproducing the original double-descent experiments.
record.gate_note: The study also reports loss-landscape sharpness, gradient norms, switching from Mixup to ERM, and covariate-shift evaluations. Sharpness and gradient norm are not measures of the listed versions. Switching experiments evaluate a training workaround rather than the unmodified Mixup trajectory. Covariate-shift results are included because they report test performance across training epochs. Values given only in figures are recorded as figure only.
record.test_reason: It tracks deep-network test error over training epochs (the V2 measure) under Mixup, a new setting. It reports only a fall-then-rise U-shape with no second descent within 1600–7000 epochs, so it bears on V2 only partially. The authors frame this as Mixup-noise overfitting, not double descent.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that Mixup over-training can yield a U-shaped generalization curve, worse with smaller datasets. They attribute it to Mixup-induced data-dependent label noise: clean patterns are fit early and noise later. They also show that switching from Mixup to ERM at the right time avoids the degradation. They do not claim a second descent or double descent for Mixup.
record.recipe_differences: The study investigates Mixup over-training, using synthetic interpolated examples and test performance across training durations; it does not reproduce model-size or sample-size interpolation sweeps from the cited double-descent work. For the main experiments, each endpoint is obtained by a separate training trial, and the reported test result is at the checkpoint with minimum training loss.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported turning point changes with dataset size, data augmentation, the Mixup coefficient/noise level, and selected RegMixup settings. The reported trend also differs across covariate-shift test sets.

fits_no_version.finding: Mixup-induced data-dependent label noise produces a fall-then-rise (U-shaped) test-loss curve over training. In theory and in a toy random-feature model, higher noise (λ near 0.5) moves the turning point earlier.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training on noisy-label synthetic data in an under-parameterized-relative-to-data regime yields a U-shaped epoch-wise risk curve, with turning-point timing set by noise level and eigenvalue scale ηµ.

fits_no_version.finding: RegMixup with η=0.1 postpones but does not remove the over-training degradation; with η=2 it matches Mixup.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mixing in clean-data loss delays but does not eliminate Mixup over-training degradation.

fits_no_version.finding: Covariate-shift accuracy of Mixup checkpoints declines on CIFAR10.1/10.2 but not on CIFAR10-C. On CIFAR10-C severity 5 it keeps improving.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mixup over-training degradation depends on the type of distribution shift.

record.problems: Many plotted outcomes are provided without numeric values in the text. The CIFAR100 U-shaped testing-loss curve is reported from a single trial. The study notes large testing-accuracy variance beyond 1000 epochs for ResNet18 on SVHN. The main endpoint procedure uses separate trials and selects the checkpoint with minimum training loss, rather than simply reporting every checkpoint on one uninterrupted run. The proposed noise explanation is empirically examined in a toy regression setup and theoretically analyzed under regression assumptions; the authors note that this may not perfectly explain the classification experiments.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports additional switching-from-Mixup-to-ERM curves (Figure 6), MSE experiments (Figure 13), and gradient-norm and loss-landscape results (Figures 2, 8, 9, and 14). They are omitted because the switching curves test a workaround, MSE figures do not add a distinct result beyond the toy U-shaped Mixup evidence, and gradient norm/loss-landscape measures do not measure a listed claim version.

untested.parts: Whether a second descent follows the rise (training horizons up to 1600/7000 epochs show none). Label-noise ERM epoch-wise double descent is not run.
No test of more samples raising error. Data size only shifts the U-curve turning point.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
No double-descent peak is measured. There is no triple or multiple descent and no optimally tuned regularization; the noise result concerns a U-curve rise.

missing.what: Testing loss over epochs for 100/50/30/10% training data on CIFAR10 and SVHN. Smaller data gives an earlier U-curve turning point. Not declared in rows_left_out.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked many fall-then-rise rows to V2 as 'observed'. V2 requires fall-rise-fall, and no second descent is reported, so these rows are downgraded to partial. Main-experiment values come from separate trials per endpoint, taking test accuracy at the minimum-training-loss checkpoint; all values are figure-only. Toy, theory, RegMixup and covariate-shift rows are unlinked: they concern a U-curve rise, not a double-descent peak. The reader's V6 supports label has no basis.

versions.untested_parts: Model-size sweeps and test error near a model-size interpolation threshold.
The study tests epoch-wise test performance for Mixup and selected controls, not whether the same curve holds generally across deep networks or training procedures.
It varies dataset size and reports changes in the timing of deterioration, but does not test whether increasing sample size near an interpolation threshold raises test error.
No capacity sweep across model classes or test of the general risk curve past interpolation.
No single effective-complexity measure is used to predict peak locations across axes.
The study examines Mixup-induced noise and selected noise/regularization settings, but does not test triple or multiple descent, or whether optimally tuned regularization eliminates the peak.
No re-counting of complexity by an effective number of parameters.

relationships.condition: Mixup (α=1) over-training of ResNet18/34 and VGG16 on CIFAR10/100 and SVHN, with and without augmentation
relationships.reason: Test error falls then rises but no second descent appears within 1000–7000 epochs (r1–r13). The authors argue the synthetic set exceeds parameter count, so interpolation is not reached.
relationships.display_finding: Test error fell then rose without a second descent within 1000–7000 epochs; the authors attributed this to a synthetic dataset exceeding model parameter size, preventing interpolation.
